https://business-review.eu/lifestyle/art.text: Picasso en visite exhibition to open in Timișoara on September 17 A total of 69 works by Pablo Picasso from the collection of the Musée Picasso in Antibes will be shown in Timișoara as part of a special exhibition inaugurating Art Encounters’ new space. Tickets are now available online. Between September 17, 2026 and January 17, 2027, Art Encounters will present Picasso en visite, one of Romania’s major exhibitions this autumn, offering visitors an encounter with Pablo Picasso’s artistic universe through 69 works including paintings, drawings, engravings, lithographs, and ceramics from the collection of the Musée Picasso in Antibes. The exhibition takes as its starting point a distinctive period in the artist’s life and work. In 1946, Picasso was invited to work in the rooms of the Château Grimaldi, which at the time housed the region’s museum of history and archaeology. The artist had long dreamed of a place where he could work on a different scale from that allowed by his studio. The Mediterranean light, the sea, Greek mythology, and the atmosphere of southern France became deeply embedded in his imagination during a period of extraordinary creative freedom. The works shown in Timișoara invite visitors to discover this unique world. Tickets available online Tickets can be purchased online at bilete.artencounters.ro and through the Entertix platform. To give visitors sufficient time and space to engage with the works, while also ensuring their protection, access to the exhibition will be organised in timed slots with a limited number of visitors. Advance booking is recommended. Read more about Art Encounters to open new art centre in Timișoara with “Picasso en visite” exhibition read more Ticket prices: ● Adults aged 18–64: RON 65 (Tuesday–Thursday) / RON 75 (Friday–Sunday) ● Children aged 8–17: RON 20 / RON 25 ● Family ticket (2 adults + 2 children): RON 150 / RON 175 ● Seniors aged 65+ and students up to 26: RON 35 / RON 45 ● Private tour for two people: RON 500 Admission is free for children under eight accompanied by an adult, people with disabilities or reduced mobility and their companions, members of the press, and holders of AICA, ICOM, and ICOMOS cards, subject to prior booking at contact@artencounters.ro. One free-admission day per month On the last Tuesday of every month, the exhibition can be visited free of charge between 10:00 and 20:00. Tickets for these days will be available from the Art Encounters ticket office on the same morning, subject to availability. Guided tours Guided tours will be available in Romanian and selected foreign languages, subject to advance booking. Art Encounters will also organise free visits for school groups, with details about the programme and registration to be announced soon. Further information is available at artencounters.ro. PICASSO EN VISITE September 17, 2026 – January 17, 2027 Tuesday–Sunday | 10:00–20:00 Art Encounters | 46C Take Ionescu Blvd., Timișoara Information, tickets, and catalogue pre-orders: artencounters.ro The Art Encounters Foundation is supported by Banca Transilvania as strategic partner. The exhibition is also made possible with the support of Catena, exhibition partner, and Dedeman, education partner, alongside the Alber Foundation, which supports the educational programme dedicated to children and young people. Deloitte is the editorial partner, while the events programme is supported by Ploom and Conceptual Lab. The project also benefits from the support of ISHO and Bosch. https://www.dw.com/en/drone-sightings-br.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Mtf1 Drone sightings forced Luxembourg's only international airport to briefly suspend flights overnight [FILE: August 11, 2026] Image: Steven Mohr/SNS/picture alliance Advertisement Luxembourg authorities are investigating drone sightings that forced the country's main airport to temporarily suspend flights overnight, Prime Minister Luc Frieden said on Saturday. Frieden said Luxembourg was working with its NATO allies following the incident, which comes amid heightened European concern over suspected hybrid attacks linked to Russia . What happened at Luxembourg airport? National carrier Luxair said more than 1,800 passengers were affected, with 17 incoming flights diverted to airports including Brussels, Paris and Frankfurt . Flights resumed on Saturday, although Luxair warned that delays and knock-on disruption could continue. The airport said the closure was a precautionary measure to protect passengers, airline crews, airport employees and aircraft. Frieden stressed that it was too early to determine who was responsible. "We are analyzing the situation," Frieden told a televised press conference after an emergency meeting with the country's defense and interior ministers. Have other drones been spotted? Frieden said "potentially larger drones" had also been observed in Luxembourg's airspace in recent days. "This is new for Luxembourg, but it is not completely new for our neighboring countries," he said. "We will ensure, together with our partners, that we can guarantee the security of our populations," Frieden said. European governments have repeatedly warned of Russian-linked hybrid activities since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Such incidents have included suspected sabotage, cyberattacks and unauthorized drone flights. There is currently no evidence establishing who was responsible for the Luxembourg sightings. Home Reviews By Title By Author By Genre By Date Authors Features Regular Features Author Spotlights Bets On "Bookreporter Talks To" Videos & Podcasts "Bookaccino Live: A Lively Talk About Books" Favorite Monthly Lists & Picks Seasonal Features Awards Book Festivals Sports Features Bookshelves Coming Soon Contests Blog Newsletters Weekly Update On Sale This Week Fall Reading Summer Reading Spring Reading Winter Reading Holiday Cheer Connect Poll Word of Mouth Submitting a Book for Review Write the Editor You are here: Home Reviews The Hollow: A Bosch Novel The Hollow: A Bosch Novel Review The Hollow: A Bosch Novel It is hard to believe that THE HOLLOW is the 26th book featuring Harry Bosch. It seems just as fresh as the first one as Bosch continues to be one of the most fascinating characters in all of crime fiction. He has spawned two different streaming series, and this latest novel also inserts two other Michael Connelly characters who have seen success on the small screen: Mickey “The Lincoln Lawyer” Haller and Renée Ballard. Similar to James Patterson’s recent Alex Cross thriller, THE FAMILY CROSS, THE HOLLOW delves into Bosch’s troubled youth growing up in the California foster care system and provides us with a side and connection to a character we thought we knew that has gone unseen over decades of bestselling novels. "There is so much to love about THE HOLLOW, and I can go on for days singing its praises. Whether you are a longtime fan of this series or a newcomer, do not miss it." This may be one of the finest books that Connelly has ever written, which is incredibly high praise considering he is one of the best writers on the planet. There are moments that will make you cry and others that will shock you to your core. That is the power that a great author like Connelly has over his readers. His plotting and ability to ramp up the intensity at every opportunity has never been more on display than it is here. The book opens with Bosch visiting the grave of a woman whose death 25 years ago he failed to avenge. He remains convinced that her husband, Gregory Talbot, was guilty, but he was unable to prove it. With the help of Renée Ballard, they set him up knowing that he might show up at the cemetery that day. Bosch leaves a flower arrangement with a mic in it. Talbot takes it and later is recorded calling his current wife to brag about how he got away with murder. Bosch returns home to find his half-brother, Mickey Haller, waiting for him. Haller has news about a huge settlement involving the victims of the MacLaren Children’s Center. Billions of dollars is being distributed to make restitution, and Bosch is in line for some of that money. Even though he decides to donate his proceeds, the memory of this notorious facility makes him recall Chops, a boy he befriended there who was brutally murdered in a crime that went unsolved and basically uninvestigated. Now, he will not rest until he has found some answers and justice for Chops. Neither Bosch nor the reader has any idea what a rollercoaster ride that opening up these 60-year-old doors will become. His initial investigation turns up various former guards and others from MacLaren, but their age and addled memories do not help much. What does make sense is a bully from back in the day who may have been responsible for Chops’ death, but Bosch has not been able to locate him. Some further digging finds that not only was Nick Stokely adopted, his name was changed to Nikolai Novak. He is a major figure in organized crime with Czech mob connections, and he was one of the killers involved in the still-unsolved Wonderland murders from when Bosch was still on the beat. Bosch’s determination to nail Novak puts him on the radar of the FBI, who is in the process of a major sting operation to take him down for dealing highly dangerous missiles to the Russians. When Bosch is asked to join the team, all hell breaks loose and things go terribly wrong before they ever have a chance to be made right. But nothing will deter him from taking down Novak in his own way and making him pay for killing Chops in the area under the stairs at MacLaren known as “the hollow.” There is so much to love about THE HOLLOW, and I can go on for days singing its praises. Whether you are a longtime fan of this series or a newcomer, do not miss it.
